# Wharf 0.5.0 host and Docker preflight research

## Scope

Session 5 adds read-only supported-host and Docker preflight checks plus the
`wharf check` command. It must not change daemon configuration, pull images,
create containers, or consume model quota.

## Decisions

- Supported platform is Ubuntu 24.04 amd64, including WSL2.
- `wharf check` is the public command and returns stable exit codes.
- `--allow-unsupported-host` overrides only platform classification and emits
  an explicit warning; Docker and capacity failures remain blocking.
- Probes are injectable so tests do not require a particular host or Docker
  daemon.

## Evidence

- [`docs/wharf-sessions.md`](../../docs/wharf-sessions.md) defines Session 5
  as supported-host and Docker preflight, with host checks, Docker readiness,
  capacity probes, and read-only behavior.
- [`docs/wharf.md`](../../docs/wharf.md) requires Docker availability, resource
  capacity, nofile and inotify limits, network readiness, and a missing-base
  image failure before launch.
- [`src/wharf/ExitCodes/ExitCode.cs`](../../src/wharf/ExitCodes/ExitCode.cs)
  provides stable unsupported-host and blocked-run codes.

## Implemented boundary

The first preflight slice uses platform, Docker daemon, and capacity probes.
The capacity probe reports available memory, disk, file descriptors, inotify
instances, and PID capacity. The Docker probe validates daemon reachability
without mutating Docker state. The service preserves probe results and applies
the platform-only override.

Network allocation and image-presence checks remain execution-adjacent and
should be connected when the image and worker sessions introduce those
inputs, without making `check` perform pulls or other paid work.
